extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark covering 9.6K human-written questions as well as 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries focusing on visual and logical reasoning over charts.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different sources. For the Pew dataset, only chart images were crawled. For the other three, the underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Charts were curated from four different online sources: Statista (statista.com), The Pew research (pewresearch.org), Our World In Data (ourworldindata.org), and Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (oecd.org).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: 23,111 questions were generated automatically from human-written chart summaries using a T5 model. A simple heuristic was developed to filter out invalid questions if the answer could not be found in the chart data table.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The test set of the machine generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were asked to focus on compositional and visual questions. For each chart, workers provided two questions with answers. The same questions were then answered by another annotator. If both workers' answers exactly matched, the answer was considered correct. Otherwise, answers were manually checked to select the final correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The agreement between the crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%. Manual checking on 500 random samples found the agreement to be 78.55% when considering typos and lexical variations.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Workers with an acceptance rate of 95% and total accomplished HITs of 5000, who also passed a pretest.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The models can be abused to mislead the public about the charts content and implications, as their output cannot be guaranteed to be correct all the time.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The T5 question generation model may generate invalid questions (incomplete or not answerable from the chart) because of the mismatch in training and test domains.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing for Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) systems.
